spans.text: Extermination complete. The last signal just disappeared.
RO, do you copy?
I—(gurgle)—copy. Can you please—(gurgle)—open the—(gurgle)—floodgate?
There are no gate controls over here though?
Dammit... The control terminal—isn't at their command center?
At least re-establish the external connection now that they're wiped out—
Arghhh... Stop wriggling, RO! I'm gonna fall into the water!
I can imagine a hundred different ways to die...but I never once expected to die from shorting out because of water...
I must ask Persica to make my next body super waterproof...
Hey, don't give up just like that! You can backup your neural cloud if you short out, but unlike you, I can't get a new body!
Suddenly, a floodgate in the distance slides open. Water starts flowing out immediately and the water level gradually falls.
Huh? The gate...opened on its own?
Has Mk46 found the switch? Ugh...the water stinks... I can't stand it. How do I switch off my olfactory system...?
Can you climb off my head first...?
But the water isn't completely gone yet. Let me stay up here for a while!
In the end, the problem was solved by annihilating all enemies. How characteristic of a certain famous Griffin Commander.
That voice...
Mr...K?
Very good. At least you didn't call me "Mr. Informant" again.
You have my thanks.
Was it you who saved us?
Me? No, I'm just a regular human being.
The floodgates can only be activated by either the control panels or an off-site hack. I can't be in two places at the same time, and electronic warfare isn't my strong suit.
Then who...?
Thank your guardian angel. You'd have been dead back in the alleys if it hadn't been for them.
Guardian...angel?
As I said, we could have a proper chat if you survived. Now we can talk.
I suppose that doesn't really matter right now...
Then...uh, do you know where Angelia is?
Are all Griffin Dolls so impatient? Shouldn't we start with the most immediate question?
...Then... How do you know the sewers so well, Mr K?
Marlohe, verify their remains.
Yes, sir.
I'll answer your questions on one condition.
I'd like to take some samples from the enemies you killed. That's what my information is worth. Well? Quite a bargain, don't you think?
Commander...right... Okay, I accept your terms. Now, can you answer my previous question?
The sewers are my escape route. I know them like the back of my hand, right down to where every single rat is. I've got to admire their persistence for chasing me this far.
I've been investigating these white things for a while now, that's why they were onto me.

I was going to draw them into the sewers and make a stealthy exit, but since you honored me with a visit, I might as well take it even further. After all, opportunities to obtain samples are hard to come by.
Who exactly...are those white enemies...?
We'll have to ask their remains. Unlike you Dolls, there's some human – or should I say human parts – under all that machinery.
Human?!
Of course, you don't have to feel guilty for firing at them. The human in there died long ago. They are driven by the power of their "faith".
F...faith...? I'm afraid I don't follow.
That's right, faith. At least that's what they proclaim.
Of course we all know that's a load of bullcrap, but it's practically a miracle to their followers.
Followers... You mean these "people" believe in something and start moving again after they die... Sounds almost like a cult...
To people beyond the wall, contracting the Eurosky Low-emission Infectious Disease is basically a death sentence.
Whoever claims to be able to cure the disease will be lauded by the truly desperate.
ELID? I've seen those...
If a person in despair is shown a sliver of hope, their desire to live can give them extraordinary power. This extraordinary power can be very easily exploited.
As long as they can live another day, it doesn't matter if they get stuffed into a mechanical shell and forced to toil away even after they die.
So...someone's been exploiting people's despair and formed a cult...
Then through the cult...they built their own army...?
Humph...cult, you say? I haven't really gotten to the bottom of it all, but I bet you aren't too far off.
No background, state-of-the-art weapons, soldiers who don't fear death. Doesn't that sound horrific?
A year ago, there was suddenly a drastic increase in the number of missing people in the Yellow Zone; at the same time, the outlying areas also saw increased violent gang activities.
Six months later, the number of missing people still showed no sign of decreasing, but gang activities started going down.
The PMC in charge of the security in the area was really pleased about that, but they didn't realize that signified the rise of a new syndicate.
We fought them a few months ago, but I never thought they'd be an organization like that... Who exactly are they? What are they after...?
Oh, that incident. I'm honestly surprised you even survived that.
Still, you withdrew in such a rush, everything was neatly buried by the time it was over.
No one can tell what they're after. All I know – it is no coincidence that they're here in Belgrade, just as it is no coincidence that you're here.
It is no coincidence...that we're here...
Take this. My gift of goodwill to Griffin.
What's inside this briefcase?
Something that may prove useful for your next operation.
Oh, and Commander? I know you're monitoring our conversation from your terminal.
I don't know what you look like, but from the way you handled the situation, I understand why so many fear you.
However, while in this city, you won't want me as an enemy, just as I don't want you as an enemy – for the time being.
In any case, my regards.
Should I say... "A pleasure to meet you," or "Welcome to Belgrade"?
I've been waiting for you.
Now then...
Angelia... Let me tell you about her adventures.
Where would you like me to start?
